lesson.sourceStem: An RN assigns care for stable medical-surgical patients. The LPN is authorized and competent to give oral medications under local scope and facility policy; the UAP has no medication-administration authorization. Which assignment is appropriate?
lesson.topic: Assigning RN, LPN, and UAP care

sources.title: NCSBN: National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation
Texas Board of Nursing: Scope and assessment FAQ

initial.question_stem: An RN assigns care for stable medical-surgical patients. The LPN is authorized and competent to give oral medications under local scope and facility policy; the UAP has no medication-administration authorization. Which assignment is appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Have the UAP provide initial teaching about a low-sodium diet

options.label: B
options.text: Have the UAP independently assess pain and decide whether treatment is effective

options.label: C
options.text: Have the LPN administer scheduled oral medications to a stable patient

options.label: D
options.text: Have the LPN independently complete the comprehensive admission assessment and establish the nursing care plan

initial.key_cue: The patient is stable, and the LPN’s medication task is authorized.
initial.why_correct_short: Scheduled oral medication administration fits the LPN’s stated scope and competency. The RN remains responsible for appropriate assignment, supervision, and follow-up.

rationales.A: Initial teaching requires nursing judgment; it is not assigned to this UAP. Reinforcing established instructions is different from developing teaching.
rationales.B: The UAP may collect and report authorized observations, but independent nursing assessment and evaluation require a licensed nurse.
rationales.D: The comprehensive assessment and independent nursing care plan require RN judgment in this scenario. An LPN may contribute focused assessments and data within local scope.

initial.one_line_fix: Match the patient and task to local scope, demonstrated competence, and supervision; collecting data is different from independent nursing judgment.

retry.question_stem: Facility policy authorizes a trained UAP to record routine observations. A stable patient reports pain. Which task can the RN delegate to this UAP?

options.label: A
options.text: Determine why the patient has pain

options.label: B
options.text: Decide whether to increase the analgesic dose

options.label: C
options.text: Evaluate the effectiveness of the nursing pain plan

options.label: D
options.text: Record the patient’s reported pain rating and promptly report it to the RN

retry.key_cue: The task is reporting a patient’s statement, not interpreting it.
retry.why_correct_short: Recording and reporting an authorized observation can be delegated. The RN uses that information to assess the patient and determine follow-up.

rationales.A: Determining the cause requires nursing assessment and judgment.
rationales.B: Changing medication dosing is not within this UAP’s role and must follow the prescription and licensed-clinician process.
rationales.C: Evaluating the nursing plan requires nursing judgment, beyond recording an observation.

retry.one_line_fix: Do not confuse collecting a reported pain score with assessing its meaning.
